original_hypothesis: The protocol's 'no universal tokenizer size' is stated as a claim about SIZE, and that is the wrong variable. A tokenizer is an input compiler: what decides whether an exact reader exists on top of it is whether its segmentation ALIGNS with the morphology's semantic units, and size is only a proxy for alignment that happens to work when the merge table is learned from the same corpus the obligation lives on. The falsifiable consequence is that at ONE fixed vocabulary size, two tokenizers differing only in alignment differ in exactness; and that a frequency-learned merge table containing every unit as a merge can still fail to be unit-aligned, because merges are applied greedily left to right and a cross-boundary occurrence of a unit's own symbol pair is merged before the in-boundary one. Separately, once the READER's own description is charged (stage B0.3 metering hostility), the cost-optimal vocabulary size must move with morphology, with the reuse horizon and with the price vector, so 'no universal tokenizer size' is a statement about three declared axes and not one.
original_prediction: see new_prediction_before_outcome: eighteen numbered clauses, C1 to C18, frozen verbatim in this record and evaluated by gmi_microscope/b2_tokenizer.py against microscopes/results/STAGE_B2_01_TOKENIZER_V1.json.
minimal_proposed_change: DECLARED module gmi_microscope/b2_tokenizer.py plus the shared charged instrument gmi_microscope/b2_common.py. Surface alphabet Sigma = {0..7}; three morphologies each declaring EIGHT semantic units of length 1, 2 and 3 symbols with values (1, 1, -2, -2, 3, 3, 0, 0); a corpus string is a concatenation of THREE units, so each of the three corpora has exactly 8^3 = 512 enumerated strings and they differ only in surface length (3, 6, 9); the obligation q(u) is the sum of the three unit values. Rows: a BPE-style merge ladder at k = 0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 merges (most frequent adjacent pair, lexicographic tie-break, applied in learned order), giving V = 8 + k; plus ORACLE_UNIT, the declared unit-aligned tokenizer whose vocabulary is the eight symbols plus the eight units; plus the rule-22 hindsight-optimal CONSTANT-answer control row. Capability of every row is the PARENT-MAXIMAL reader of its feature map (the best function of the token multiset, by plurality within each feature class), with linear realizability of the exact rational system Phi w = q reported separately. Charged serve = one operation per token served. Description charged = 2*V*d embedding/unembedding scalars at d = 4 PLUS the reader's own description (V weights if linearly realizable, one answer per feature class otherwise). Four declared price vectors (c_mem, c_len) = (1,1), (1,4), (4,1), (1,16). Cross-remint = a declared permutation pi of Sigma respelling the units and carrying their values over: the MERGE TABLE IS FROZEN, the reader is refit with hindsight. Exact rationals throughout, no floating point in any decided quantity, no randomness anywhere.
why_justified: The protocol row names four factorial axes and four endpoints and predicts only the absence of a universal optimum. Executing it needs (i) an obligation whose unit structure is declared so that alignment is a measurable quantity and not an interpretation, (ii) an admissibility rule that is parent-maximal for the feature map rather than the convenient linear one (protocol rule 19), (iii) the reader's own description charged, or a coarse tokenizer buys its exactness with an unpriced table (stage B0.3), and (iv) the constant-answer control of rule 22 and the charged-serve audit of rule 21 as narrowed by RV-377-073. PRE-FREEZE CALIBRATION, DISCLOSED IN FULL: a calibration run was executed before these clauses were frozen, on the BPE ladder alone with admissibility defined as consistency of the exact LINEAR system. It showed that no row of that ladder is linearly consistent on MORPH2 or MORPH3, leaving both ecologies with an EMPTY admissible set, and that the frequency-learned merge table crosses unit boundaries even once it contains every unit as a merge. Three changes followed, all before the freeze: admissibility moved to the parent-maximal reader; the ORACLE_UNIT arm was added so that size and alignment are separable; and the reader's description was charged. The calibration also fixed the numbers behind the predicted verdicts below - the character-level capabilities, the minimal exact vocabulary sizes and the mem1_len1 occupant sets - and it is on that basis that C17 is predicted to FAIL. C17 is frozen anyway because the quantitative claim is worth committing either way.

new_falsifier: C14 failing - the unit-aligned row being no more exact than the frequency-learned row of the same vocabulary size - would refute the alignment reading and return the row to the protocol's size reading. C15 failing - every BPE table with at least 8 merges being perfectly unit-aligned - would show that greedy left-to-right application does recover unit boundaries and would make the ORACLE_UNIT arm redundant. C4, C5 and C6 all holding at a single optimum would falsify 'no universal tokenizer size' directly. C9 failing anywhere would VOID that morphology under rule 22 and every clause evaluated on it would have to be withdrawn.

strongest_mundane_explanation: The alignment result is an artefact of the declared morphology: the units were chosen to contain surface anagrams with different values ((0,1) at value 1 against (1,0) at value 3), which is exactly what makes a symbol-count reader fail and what gives greedy merging a cross-boundary pair to consume. ACCEPTED AS A LIMIT ON THE CLAIM and stated in the claim ceiling: the result is that alignment CAN dissociate from size on a declared morphology, not that it always does. What the construction does not explain away is the size of the dissociation: on MORPH3 no frequency-learned table of up to 24 merges reaches exactness at all, while a 16-entry unit-aligned vocabulary is exact AND linear AND needs 8 labelled examples.
strongest_parent_explanation: This is the known tokenizer-alignment problem of subword segmentation: BPE optimizes a frequency objective, not a morphological one, and is known to split morphemes and to merge across boundaries (the parent literature of TF-001, Sennrich et al. 2016 for the merge construction and Kudo/Richardson 2018 for the unigram-LM alternative motivated by exactly this). That is the correct parent explanation and it is not disputed. What this record adds is that the failure is measurable as an EXACTNESS gap at MATCHED vocabulary size in a fully enumerated ecology with a charged cost model, so that the protocol's 'no universal tokenizer size' becomes a statement with a named controlling variable.
measurement_validity_status: VALID. Every corpus is enumerated in full (512 strings each), every segmentation is deterministic, every capability and cost is an exact rational, there is no randomness and no tolerance anywhere, and the capability of every row is the PARENT-MAXIMAL reader of its feature map rather than a convenient linear one (protocol rule 19). The reader's own description is charged, so no row hides a table in the tokenizer's embedding count (stage B0.3). One instrument limitation is disclosed: the charged serve model prices one operation per token served and does not price attention over the sequence, so it understates the sequence-length axis; every occupancy statement is relative to that declared price.
mechanism_attribution: Exactness is attributable to SEGMENTATION ALIGNMENT and not to vocabulary size. The mediating quantity is measured directly and reported per row as unit_aligned_segmentation_fraction; it is 1 for the character-level row and for the unit-aligned row, and strictly below 1 for every frequency-learned row with at least 8 merges on MORPH2 and MORPH3. Frontier occupancy, by contrast, is attributable to the reuse horizon and the price vector, and is where the protocol's original 'no universal size' reading lives.
new_invariant_learned: A TOKENIZER'S EXACTNESS IS A PROPERTY OF ITS SEGMENTATION BOUNDARIES, NOT OF ITS VOCABULARY SIZE, AND THE TWO CAN BE DISSOCIATED AT MATCHED SIZE. Separately, and independently: a hindsight-optimal CONSTANT answer scores 9/64 on all three morphologies, so the constant control of rule 22 is a live control here and not a formality; and a frequency-learned merge table that CONTAINS every semantic unit as a merge can still be unit-aligned on as little as 57 per cent of its corpus, because greedy left-to-right application consumes cross-boundary occurrences first.
new_theory_constraint: Registry entries TF-001 and TF-002 must state the response law in terms of ALIGNMENT with the obligation's unit structure, with vocabulary size as the resource axis rather than the capability axis; their kill conditions as written (a single vocabulary size winning on every endpoint across corpora) are untouched and remain unkilled. No new protocol rule is proposed: the record needed rules 17, 19, 21 (as narrowed), 22, 28 and 29 and none of them broke.
